Endpoint protection such as Cisco Secure Endpoint
Right. It runs on the device and watches for malicious files and behavior.
MACsec on the access port of the laptop's switch
It encrypts frames on the link and does not scan files.
An email security gateway in front of the mail server
It filters mail before delivery and does not inspect the laptop.

q.q: Which control blocks requests to known malicious domains before a connection is made, even for devices off the corporate network?
o: DNS-layer security such as Cisco Umbrella
Right. It decides at lookup time and so stops the connection before it begins.
A stateful packet filter at the data center edge
It sees only traffic that passes through that edge.
802.1X on every switch port
802.1X controls who connects to a port, not which domains are visited.
A sandbox that detonates files
Sandboxes analyze files and do not stop DNS lookups.

q.q: Some switches cannot insert an SGT into packets. How can they still learn the SGT of an IP address?
o: With BGP communities set on the access switches
BGP communities are not used to share endpoint SGT bindings.
With CDP messages that are sent on every port of the switch
CDP shares device information, and it has no SGT bindings.
With OSPF opaque LSAs flooded into area 0
OSPF does not carry SGT bindings.
With SXP, which shares IP-to-SGT bindings over TCP
Right. SXP sends the bindings between devices that cannot tag packets inline.

q.q: What does this script print?
o: sw1 and sw2, each on its own line
That would be devices[:2]. This slice starts at index 1.
Only sw2, because the slice stops after one item
The slice runs to the end of the list, not just one item.
sw2 and sw3, each on its own line
Right. The slice [1:] starts at index 1, so the first item is skipped.
An IndexError, because index 1 is out of range
Slicing does not cause an IndexError.

q.q: What happens when this code runs?
o: A KeyError, because the key user does not exist in the dictionary
Right. Reading a missing key with square brackets raises a KeyError.
An IndexError, because user is not a valid position
An IndexError is for list positions, not dictionary keys.
It prints None, as the get method would
None would be printed by the get method, not by square brackets.
It prints an empty string for the missing key
Python does not make an empty value for a missing key.

q.q: In this script, what does r.json() return?
o: The request headers as a dictionary
The request headers are what was sent, not parsed from the body.
The HTTP status code of the response, as an integer
The status code is read with r.status_code.
A JSON string made from a Python dictionary
That is what json.dumps does.
The body parsed into a Python dict or list
Right. It converts the JSON text of the reply into Python objects.
q.code:
r = requests.get(url, headers=h, verify=False)
data = r.json()

q.q: What does this code print?
o: VLAN20
That would be the result if no prefix were passed.
ENG-20
Right. The second argument replaces the default prefix, and str(vid) turns 20 into text so it can be joined.
A TypeError
The number is converted with str, so the join works.
ENG-VLAN20
The prefix argument replaces the default and is not added to it.

q.q: Which of the following is valid JSON?
o: {"name": "Gi0/1", "enabled": yes}
yes is not a JSON value. Booleans must be written true or false.
{'name': 'Gi0/1', 'enabled': true}
JSON does not allow single quotes.
{"name": "Gi0/1", "enabled": true}
Right. Keys use double quotes and true is lowercase, so this is valid.
{"name": "Gi0/1", "enabled": true,}
A trailing comma is not allowed in JSON.

q.q: After json.loads puts the text below into a variable d, which expression returns 20?
o: d["vlans"][1]["id"]
Right. vlans is a list, index 1 is the second item, and then the id key is read.
d["vlans"][2]["id"]
Index 2 would be a third item, and the list has only two.
d["vlans"]["id"][1]
A list cannot be read by a key name.
d[vlans][1][id]
The keys are strings and must be quoted.

q.q: In a YANG model, what does a node marked config false represent?
o: A node that NETCONF hides from every client
Clients can read these nodes.
Operational state that is read-only, such as counters
Right. config false marks state data. It can be read but not set through edit-config.
Data that can be changed with edit-config
Only config true nodes can be changed.
Configuration that is only applied at boot time
That is not a YANG idea. Config nodes can be changed while the device runs.

q.q: What does a YANG model describe?
o: A scripting language used to run CLI commands on many devices at once
YANG describes data, and it is not a language for running commands.
The TCP port number that clients use to reach the device's API service
Ports belong to the transport, not to the data model.
Data structure and types, independent of encoding
Right. A model describes what data a device exposes. NETCONF and RESTCONF then carry it in XML or JSON.
The XML message format that NETCONF uses on the wire between devices
YANG is not an encoding. The same model can be sent as XML or JSON.

q.q: In a YANG model, which node type holds a single value, such as an interface MTU?
o: container
A container groups other nodes.
leaf-list
A leaf-list holds several values of the same type.
list
A list holds several entries, each with a key.
leaf
Right. A leaf is one value of one type.

q.q: What is the main benefit of model-driven programmability over screen-scraping CLI output?
o: No authentication is required for model-based calls
Authentication is still required.
Commands run faster on the device CPU and use less memory
Speed depends on the device and is not the main benefit.
It works without any transport protocol such as SSH or HTTPS
Models are carried by NETCONF, RESTCONF or gNMI.
Structured data, so scripts do not parse text
Right. A script reads named fields instead of guessing at column positions.

q.q: Which Catalyst Center API would an app use to read the device inventory or request a change in the network?
o: The multivendor SDK, a southbound interface
That is how Catalyst Center talks to devices, not how apps talk to it.
SNMP traps from the appliance
Traps are sent for events and are not an interface for reading inventory.
The Intent API, a northbound REST API
Right. It gives applications access to Catalyst Center functions through REST calls.
The CLI of each device
Direct CLI use does not go through Catalyst Center.

q.q: SD-WAN Manager REST calls begin with which path?
o: /dataservice
Right. The SD-WAN Manager REST API lives under /dataservice.
/restconf/data
That is the RESTCONF path on a device.
/api/v2/network
This is not the SD-WAN Manager path.
/dna/intent/api/v1
That is the Catalyst Center intent API path.

q.q: A Catalyst Center API call that changes the network returns 202 and a taskId. What should the script do next?
o: Treat the change as complete, since 202 means success
A 202 only means the work was queued.
Poll the task API with the taskId until it finishes
Right. A 202 means the request was accepted, and the result is known only when the task completes.
Send the same request again to confirm it was accepted
Repeating a request can create duplicate work.
Switch to RESTCONF on the device to read the result
The task result is read from the Catalyst Center task API.

q.q: A script holds a valid token, but a request to delete a site returns 403. What does that mean?
o: The site does not exist on the controller
A missing resource gives 404.
The JSON body is malformed or has a missing field
A malformed request gives 400.
The account is known but not allowed to do this
Right. 403 Forbidden means the server knows who you are and refuses the action.
The token has expired and must be requested again
An expired or missing token gives 401.

q.q: A RESTCONF PUT replaces an existing interface description and the change succeeds. Which response is expected?
o: 204 No Content
Right. When an existing resource is replaced, the server returns 204 with no body.
404 Not Found, because the interface is missing
The resource exists, so it is found.
409 Conflict, because the data already exists
A conflict means the request clashes with the existing data.
201 Created, because the resource was made
201 is returned when the PUT creates a new resource.

q.q: A RESTCONF POST tries to create Loopback99, which already exists. Which status does the device return?
o: 400 Bad Request
The request is well formed. The problem is that the data already exists.
409 Conflict
Right. The data already exists, so the create request conflicts with it.
201 Created
201 is returned when a new resource was created.
404 Not Found
The resource exists, so it is found.

q.q: An API call with valid credentials and a correct body returns 500. What does that tell you?
o: The credentials are wrong, so request a new token
Bad credentials give 401.
The request was malformed, so fix the JSON
A malformed request gives 400.
The URL points to a missing resource, so check the path
A missing resource gives 404.
The server failed while handling a valid request, so retry later or escalate
Right. 5xx codes mean a server-side error.

q.q: When does this EEM applet run?
o: Every 2 minutes
That would need a different cron entry.
At 02:00 on the first of each month
That would need 1 in the day-of-month field.
Only when started by hand
A manual start uses the event none trigger.
Every day at 02:00
Right. The cron entry 0 2 * * * means minute 0, hour 2, every day.
q.code:
event manager applet NIGHTLY
 event timer cron cron-entry "0 2 * * *"
 action 1.0 cli command "enable"
 action 2.0 cli command "show ip interface brief | append flash:ints.txt"

q.q: Which EEM event detector starts an applet when a specific log message appears?
o: event syslog pattern
Right. It matches log messages against a pattern and runs the actions.
event snmp oid, which watches an SNMP object
It reacts to the value of an SNMP object, not to a log message.
event none
It lets the applet be started only by a manual command.
event timer cron, which runs on a schedule
It runs on a schedule.

q.q: An applet uses event none. How is it started?
o: It starts when any CLI command is typed
That needs an event cli trigger.
With event manager run and the applet name
Right. The none event waits for a manual run.
It starts when the router reloads or its config is saved
A reload is not what event none waits for.
It starts at the next syslog message
That needs an event syslog trigger.

q.q: An agent on each managed server contacts its configuration server every 30 minutes and downloads its settings. Which model is this?
o: An event-driven model only
Nothing here is triggered by an event. The agent checks in on a timer.
An out-of-band model
Out-of-band describes the management path, not who starts the exchange.
A pull model
Right. The managed node asks the server for its configuration. Puppet and Chef agents work this way.
A push model
In a push model the control node connects out to the devices on demand.

q.q: In which format are Ansible playbooks written?
o: Ruby, as recipes
That is how Chef recipes are written.
HCL
That is the language used for Terraform.
YAML
Right. Playbooks are YAML files listing tasks to run on hosts.
XML
Playbooks use YAML and not XML.

q.q: Why does Ansible work well for network devices that cannot run extra software?
o: It pulls its configuration from a master every 30 minutes
That is how agent-based tools such as Puppet behave.
It needs a Python agent installed on every switch it manages
That is not required.
It works only on Linux hosts, not on network devices
Ansible manages many network platforms.
It connects over SSH or APIs, so no agent is needed
Right. This agentless design suits switches and routers.

q.q: Which TWO statements describe a two-tier collapsed core design? (Choose two.)
o: Access switches connect straight to the WAN router
Access switches connect to the distribution and core pair, not directly to the WAN router.
Distribution and core functions run on one redundant pair of switches
Right. The collapsed core pair does both jobs, so there is no separate core layer.
It removes the need for redundant uplinks from the access switches
Access switches still need redundant uplinks to the pair.
It suits a small campus served by one pair
Right. A single pair is enough when the campus is small, which keeps cost and cabling down.
Each building needs its own separate core layer
A separate core per building is the opposite of collapsing the layers.

q.q: Which TWO statements about VRF-lite are correct? (Choose two.)
o: VRF-lite requires MPLS labels on every link
Labels are used by MPLS VPNs. VRF-lite does not need them.
All VRFs share one routing table and are separated by VLAN tags
They do not share a table.
An interface belongs to one VRF at a time
Right. An interface is assigned to one VRF, or to the global table.
The same prefix may not be used in two VRFs
Overlapping prefixes are allowed because the tables are separate.
Each VRF has its own routing table, so the same prefix can exist in two VRFs
Right. Separate tables are the whole point, so the same prefix can exist in two VRFs.

q.q: Which TWO statements about the OSPF point-to-point network type are correct? (Choose two.)
o: Hello and dead timers default to 10 and 40 seconds
Right. These are the defaults on point-to-point links, as on broadcast networks.
Neighbors must be configured by hand with the neighbor command
Hellos are multicast and find neighbors on their own.
The default hello interval is 30 seconds
30 seconds is the default on non-broadcast networks.
No DR or BDR is elected
Right. The two routers on the link become adjacent directly, so no election is needed.
A DR is elected using the highest priority
DR election belongs to the broadcast network type.

q.q: Which TWO statements about local SPAN on a Catalyst switch are correct? (Choose two.)
o: Traffic routed between VLANs is captured by a VLAN source
Inter-VLAN routed traffic is not monitored by VLAN-based SPAN.
The destination port cannot be an EtherChannel
Right. The destination must be a physical port.
Source ports and source VLANs can be mixed in one session
They cannot be mixed. A session uses one type or the other.
The destination port cannot also be one of the source ports
Right. A destination is dedicated to the session and is not monitored.
A destination port can serve several sessions at once
A destination port serves only one session at a time.

q.q: Which TWO statements about ACL processing are correct? (Choose two.)
o: A standard ACL can match the destination port
Standard ACLs match only the source address.
An implicit deny ends every ACL
Right. Packets that match no line are dropped.
Entries are checked from the top, and the first match decides
Right. After a match, the remaining entries are not checked.
A 1 bit in a wildcard mask means the bit must match
It is the reverse. A 0 bit must match and a 1 bit is ignored.
An outbound ACL filters packets the router itself generates
Outbound ACLs do not filter traffic that the router originates.

q.q: A script runs json.dumps({'up': True, 'mtu': None}). What text does it produce?
o: {"up": true, "mtu": null}
Right. dumps converts Python True to true and None to null, and uses double quotes.
{'up': True, 'mtu': None}
That is how Python prints the dictionary. JSON text does not use single quotes or Python names.
{"up": True, "mtu": None}
The keys are quoted, but True and None are not valid JSON values.
{"up": "true", "mtu": "null"}
The values would become strings, but dumps keeps booleans and null as real JSON values.

q.q: Which TWO things can an EEM applet do? (Choose two.)
o: Send a syslog message when its event occurs
Right. A syslog action is one of the standard applet actions.
Install a Python agent into the router operating system
Applets run CLI and logging actions. They do not install software agents.
Create new YANG models for the device
Models come from the platform software, not from an applet.
Change the configuration of neighboring routers directly
An applet acts on the device that runs it.
Run CLI commands, such as a show command, and save the output to a file
Right. A cli command action runs on the local device, and the output can go to flash.

q.q: Catalyst Center's AI-powered workflow suggests a fix for a problem that keeps returning on two core switches. What should the operator do first?
o: Apply the suggestion to the two affected switches now, since it came from Assurance telemetry
Telemetry is not approval. A change to core switches still needs review and an approved change.
Review the suggestion and its impact, then apply it by the normal change process
Right. An AI suggestion is advice. The operator still checks the effect and gets the change approved before a core device is touched.
Open a TAC case before reading the suggestion
Reading the suggestion is the first step. A TAC case may come later if the review shows a real need.
Mark the issue resolved so the AI learns the fix
Closing the issue does not fix anything, and the problem would come back unnoticed.

q.q: What happens to SSH packets that arrive at the router faster than 64 kb/s?
o: The excess is dropped before it reaches the route processor
Right. The police command drops traffic over the rate on the control-plane input policy.
The excess is queued and sent later
Queuing and delay is shaping. This policy uses police with an exceed action of drop.
All SSH traffic through the router is limited to 64 kb/s
The policy is on the control plane and only counts packets sent to the router.
The excess is forwarded with a lower priority mark
Re-marking needs an exceed action of set-dscp. This one drops.
q.code:
ip access-list extended SSH-IN
 permit tcp any any eq 22
class-map match-all COPP-SSH
 match access-group name SSH-IN
policy-map COPP
 class COPP-SSH
  police 64000 conform-action transmit exceed-action drop
control-plane
 service-policy input COPP

q.q: Which protocol negotiates and distributes the keys that two devices use for MACsec on a link?
o: MKA, the MACsec Key Agreement protocol
Right. MKA runs after 802.1X or a pre-shared key and sets up the session keys.
SXP, which shares IP-to-SGT bindings
SXP shares IP-to-SGT bindings and does not carry keys.
LACP, which bundles links together
LACP bundles links and has nothing to do with encryption keys.
IKEv2, which sets up IPsec tunnels
IKEv2 sets up IPsec tunnels. MACsec uses MKA.

q.q: The ACL below is applied inbound on the outside interface. An outside host opens a new TCP connection to a lab server. What happens?
o: It is denied and logged, because a first packet has SYN but no ACK
Right. The established keyword matches only segments with ACK or RST, so a new connection falls to the deny line.
It is permitted by the first line, because it is TCP
The first line permits only TCP segments that already have ACK or RST set.
It is permitted, because ACLs track connections on their own
A plain ACL does not track state.
It is dropped without being logged
The final line includes the log keyword.
q.code:
ip access-list extended OUT-IN
 permit tcp any any established
 permit udp any eq 53 any
 deny ip any any log

q.q: What does access-class MGMT-ONLY in do on these vty lines?
o: Only hosts that the ACL permits can open sessions to the lines
Right. The access-class filters who may connect to the vty lines.
It decides which users may enter enable mode
Privilege access is decided by the enable secret or AAA, not by this ACL.
It filters user traffic passing through the router to the management subnet
Access-class applies to sessions to the router, not to transit traffic.
It encrypts the sessions to the lines
Encryption comes from SSH, which transport input ssh requires.
q.code:
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh
 exec-timeout 5 0
 access-class MGMT-ONLY in

q.title: Plan an HSRP-safe upgrade of the active switch
q.scenario: In the unit's lab, DS1 (HSRP active, priority 110) and DS2 (standby, priority 100) share the gateway 10.10.10.1 for VLAN 10 in HSRP group 10. Neither has preempt. The approved change is to upgrade DS1's software without losing the gateway. Build the plan in the right order. Some ideas do not belong.
q.ticket: CHG-5530 (lab): upgrade DS1 during the approved window. The gateway must stay up. Roll back if hosts lose 10.10.10.1.

rules.text: Copy both running configs to flash and note the rollback steps
rules.why: A saved copy and a written rollback let you undo the change fast if the gateway is lost.

rules.text: Check show standby brief: DS2 must be Standby and ready
rules.why: Moving the gateway to a switch that is not ready would cause the outage you are trying to avoid.

rules.text: Raise DS2's priority above DS1 and enable preempt so DS2 becomes active
rules.why: This moves the gateway to DS2 on purpose, so DS1 can be upgraded without users noticing.

rules.text: Confirm DS2 shows Active and a test host still pings 10.10.10.1
rules.why: Proof that traffic flows through DS2 tells you it is safe to take DS1 down.
With DS2 active and tested, the reload of DS1 no longer affects the gateway.

rules.text: When DS1 is back in the group, return DS2's priority and preempt settings to what they were
rules.why: This puts the design back to its approved state so a later change starts from known settings.

rules.text: Record the result in the change ticket
rules.why: The ticket must show what was done and that the gateway stayed up.

rules.text: Shut down DS1's uplinks first and watch whether HSRP reacts
rules.why: This is an unplanned failover test. Users lose service while you wait to see what happens.

rules.text: Lower DS1's priority to 90 and leave preempt off on DS2
rules.why: With no preempt on DS2, DS1 stays active even at priority 90, so the gateway does not move and DS1 still goes down with the gateway on it.

rules.text: Turn off HSRP on DS2 so it cannot interfere
rules.why: DS2 is the switch that carries the gateway while DS1 is down. Turning HSRP off there removes the backup.

before.why: Back up and write the rollback before the first configuration change.
Check that DS2 is ready before you force the gateway onto it.
You can only confirm DS2 is active after you have made it active.
Do not reload DS1 until DS2 is proven to carry the gateway.
Restoring settings makes sense only once DS1 has come back.

last.why: Documenting comes last because the ticket must show the finished result.
